# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Fuhr_2022_felodipine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Fuhr_2022_felodipine"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics14071474> (open access, PMC9322514)
* Supplement: <https://www.mdpi.com/article/10.3390/pharmaceutics14071474/s1>
  (reference manual; Section 1.6 gives the PD equations S16-S22, Tables S5 and
  S6 the PD parameters)

Felodipine is a dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker whose blood-pressure
effect tracks its plasma concentration directly. Fuhr 2022 built a
parent-metabolite PBPK model of felodipine and dehydrofelodipine in PK-Sim /
MoBi (Open Systems Pharmacology Suite 9.1) and extended it with a PD model of
diastolic blood pressure (DBP) and heart rate (HR). The PBPK model was then
used to predict CYP3A4 drug-drug interactions with erythromycin, itraconazole,
carbamazepine and phenytoin.

**Only the PD layer is packaged here.** The PBPK layer is a platform
whole-body model: its organ volumes, blood flows, tissue partition
coefficients (Rodgers-Rowland / Schmitt methods) and CYP3A4 expression profile
are PK-Sim database outputs that the paper does not tabulate, so it cannot be
rebuilt from the publication. The PD layer, by contrast, is printed in full
(supplementary Equations S16-S22, main-text Table 3). Its only input from the
PBPK layer is the felodipine plasma concentration. Here that concentration is
supplied by the user as the time-varying covariate `CEFFECT` (umol/L).

# Population

The PD layer was built from 30 DBP-time and 22 HR-time profiles taken from
17 published clinical studies (Results 3.2; Table 1). Of these, 18 DBP and
18 HR profiles came from healthy volunteers and 12 DBP and 4 HR profiles from
patients with essential hypertension, many of whom were also taking other
antihypertensives (supplementary Table S1, footnote c). Felodipine was given
as 1-3 mg intravenous infusions or as 0.83-40 mg oral solution,
immediate-release tablet or extended-release tablet, in single or multiple
doses. All data are means digitised from the literature. No individual data
were used, so the total number of individuals is not reported. The
healthy-volunteer cohorts in Table S1 are mostly young men (per-study mean
ages 24-33 years); the hypertensive cohorts are older.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Fuhr_2022_felodipine")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `circ_dbp` (24 h + 12 h cosinor) | n/a | Supplement Eq. S16 (structure from Chae et al., ref. 28) |
| `dbp = e0_dbp * (1 + circ_dbp) - eff_dbp` | n/a | Supplement Eq. S17 and S21 |
| `circ_hr` (24 h cosinor) | n/a | Supplement Eq. S18 (structure from Lott et al., ref. 29) |
| `hr = e0_hr * (1 + circ_hr) + eff_hr` | n/a | Supplement Eq. S19 and S22 |
| `eff = emax * C^h / (ec50^h + C^h)` | n/a | Main-text Eq. 1 = supplement Eq. S20 |
| `lemax_dbp` | log(56.18 mmHg) | Table 3 (and Table S6), DBP Emax |
| `lec50_dbp` | log(0.04 umol/L) | Table 3, DBP EC50; "40 nmol/L" in the Discussion |
| DBP Hill coefficient | 1 (not a parameter) | Table 3 lists `h` for the HR model only |
| `amp24_dbp` | 0.0214 (fixed) | Table 3, amp24 = 2.14 % (literature, ref. 28) |
| `amp12_dbp` | 0.0593 (fixed) | Table 3, amp12 = 5.93 % (literature, ref. 28) |
| `phase24_dbp` | 5.28 h | Table 3, mean (SD 2.10) of per-study values |
| `phase12_dbp` | 0.16 h | Table 3, mean (SD 2.10) of per-study values |
| `le0_dbp` | log(70.4 mmHg) | Table 3, BPmean, healthy individuals |
| `e_hypert_e0_dbp` | log(91.9 / 70.4) | Table 3, BPmean for hypertensive individuals (footnote b) |
| `lemax_hr` | log(39.71 bpm) | Table 3, HR Emax |
| `lec50_hr` | log(0.05 umol/L) | Table 3, HR EC50 |
| `lhill_hr` | log(1.40) | Table 3, HR Hill coefficient |
| `amp_hr` | 0.063 (fixed) | Table 3, amp = 6.3 % (literature, ref. 29) |
| `phase_hr` | 11.8 h | Table 3, mean (SD 5.13) of per-study values |
| `le0_hr` | log(62.2 bpm) | Table 3, HRmean, healthy individuals |
| `e_hypert_e0_hr` | log(66.4 / 62.2) | Table 3, HRmean for hypertensive individuals (footnote b) |
| `addSd_dbp`, `addSd_hr` | 0 (fixed) | No residual-error model reported |
| Per-study BPmean, HRmean and phases | Table S5 | Used below to replicate Figure 4 |
| Felodipine molecular weight | 384.25 g/mol | Table 2 (converts ng/mL to umol/L) |

# Deterministic structure checks

The model has no random effects, so every check below is exact.

```{r structure}
mod <- readModelDb("Fuhr_2022_felodipine")
mw <- 384.25 # g/mol, Fuhr 2022 Table 2

grid <- expand.grid(
  time = seq(0, 24, by = 0.25),
  CEFFECT = c(0, 0.04, 0.05),
  DIS_HYPERT = c(0, 1)
)
ev_grid <- grid |>
  mutate(id = as.integer(interaction(CEFFECT, DIS_HYPERT, drop = TRUE)), evid = 0, amt = 0) |>
  arrange(id, time)
sim_grid <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod, ev_grid, keep = c("DIS_HYPERT")))

# Placebo 24 h means equal the Table 3 BPmean / HRmean values: the cosine
# harmonics average to zero over a whole 24 h period.
placebo_means <- sim_grid |>
  filter(CEFFECT == 0, time < 24) |>
  group_by(DIS_HYPERT) |>
  summarise(dbp_mean = mean(dbp), hr_mean = mean(hr), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(placebo_means, digits = 3)
stopifnot(
  abs(placebo_means$dbp_mean[placebo_means$DIS_HYPERT == 0] - 70.4) < 1e-6,
  abs(placebo_means$dbp_mean[placebo_means$DIS_HYPERT == 1] - 91.9) < 1e-6,
  abs(placebo_means$hr_mean[placebo_means$DIS_HYPERT == 0] - 62.2) < 1e-6,
  abs(placebo_means$hr_mean[placebo_means$DIS_HYPERT == 1] - 66.4) < 1e-6
)

# At CEFFECT = EC50 the drug effect is exactly Emax / 2 at every time point.
eff <- sim_grid |>
  filter(CEFFECT > 0) |>
  select(time, CEFFECT, DIS_HYPERT, eff_dbp, eff_hr)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(eff$eff_dbp[eff$CEFFECT == 0.04] - 56.18 / 2) < 1e-8),
  all(abs(eff$eff_hr[eff$CEFFECT == 0.05] - 39.71 / 2) < 1e-8)
)
```

# Exposure-response with the Table 3 typical values

```{r er-curves, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5}
conc_nM <- c(0, 10^seq(-1, 3, length.out = 120))
ev_er <- data.frame(
  id = seq_along(conc_nM), time = 0, evid = 0, amt = 0,
  CEFFECT = conc_nM / 1000, DIS_HYPERT = 0
)
sim_er <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod, ev_er))
sim_er |>
  mutate(conc_nM = CEFFECT * 1000) |>
  filter(conc_nM > 0) |>
  select(conc_nM, `DBP decrease (mmHg)` = eff_dbp, `HR increase (beats/min)` = eff_hr) |>
  pivot_longer(-conc_nM) |>
  ggplot(aes(conc_nM, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(
    data = data.frame(
      name = c("DBP decrease (mmHg)", "HR increase (beats/min)"),
      ec50 = c(40, 50)
    ),
    aes(xintercept = ec50), linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Felodipine plasma concentration (nmol/L)", y = "Drug effect",
    caption = "Dashed lines: EC50 (Fuhr 2022 Table 3)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

At 20 nmol/L (about 7.7 ng/mL), a typical peak after a 10-20 mg
extended-release tablet, the model predicts a DBP decrease of
`r round(56.18 * 0.02 / (0.04 + 0.02), 1)` mmHg and an HR increase of
`r round(39.71 * 0.02^1.4 / (0.05^1.4 + 0.02^1.4), 1)` beats/min.

# Replicating Figure 4

Figure 4 of Fuhr 2022 shows, for three studies, the PBPK-predicted felodipine
plasma concentration (panels a-c) together with the predicted DBP (d-f) and
HR (g-i) curves. Panels a, d-i are vector graphics in the article PDF. The
maintainers extracted the model-prediction lines from the vector paths, with
each axis calibrated on its tick marks, and resampled them onto a common time
grid. Panels b and c are embedded raster images and were not digitised. The
curves below are therefore the paper's own predictions, not observed data.

Fuhr 2022 re-optimised the 24 h means and phases for every simulated study.
Each replication therefore overrides the Table 3 means with that study's
Table S5 values:

* Edgar 1987 (healthy, oral solution 5 / 15 / 40 mg): BPmean 69.57 mmHg,
  phase12 0.95 h, phase24 6.07 h; HRmean 56.81 bpm, phaseHR 18.48 h.
* Blychert 1990 (hypertensive, 20 mg extended-release tablet once daily, day
  15): BPmean 95.88 mmHg, phase12 1.01 h, phase24 6.13 h; HRmean 60.92 bpm,
  phaseHR 15.24 h.
* Hedner 1986 (hypertensive, 5 then 10 mg tablet twice daily, day 28):
  BPmean 87.70 mmHg, phase12 -0.02 h, phase24 5.10 h; HRmean 66.13 bpm,
  phaseHR 13.63 h.

Because these per-study means replace `le0_dbp` and `le0_hr` directly,
`DIS_HYPERT` is kept at 0 in every replication. Setting it to 1 would apply
the Table 3 hypertensive/healthy ratio a second time.

```{r study-models}
# Override the cross-study Table 3 means with one study's Table S5 values.
study_model <- function(bp_mean, phase12, phase24, hr_mean, phase_hr) {
  rxode2::ini(
    mod,
    le0_dbp = log(bp_mean), phase12_dbp = phase12, phase24_dbp = phase24,
    le0_hr = log(hr_mean), phase_hr = phase_hr
  )
}
mod_edgar <- study_model(69.57, 0.95, 6.07, 56.81, 18.48)
mod_blychert <- study_model(95.88, 1.01, 6.13, 60.92, 15.24)
mod_hedner <- study_model(87.70, -0.02, 5.10, 66.13, 13.63)
```

## Healthy volunteers: Edgar 1987 (panels a, d, g)

The digitised predicted plasma concentrations of panel a (ng/mL, converted to
umol/L with the Table 2 molecular weight) drive the model directly. Placebo is
`CEFFECT = 0`. `DIS_HYPERT` stays 0 here because the study-specific means
already replace the Table 3 values.

```{r edgar}
edgar_long <- edgar |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = c("var", "arm"), names_sep = "_") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = var, values_from = value)
arms <- c("placebo", "5", "15", "40")
# The paper's curves are kept out of the event table so that their dbp / hr
# columns cannot be mistaken for model inputs.
ev_edgar <- edgar_long |>
  transmute(
    id = match(arm, arms), time,
    CEFFECT = ifelse(arm == "placebo", 0, conc / mw),
    evid = 0, amt = 0, DIS_HYPERT = 0
  ) |>
  arrange(id, time)
sim_edgar <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod_edgar, ev_edgar)) |>
  mutate(arm = arms[id])

cmp_edgar <- edgar_long |>
  select(arm, time, dbp_paper = dbp, hr_paper = hr) |>
  left_join(select(sim_edgar, arm, time, dbp, hr), by = c("arm", "time")) |>
  mutate(dbp_diff = dbp - dbp_paper, hr_diff = hr - hr_paper)
stopifnot(nrow(cmp_edgar) == nrow(ev_edgar), !anyNA(cmp_edgar$dbp))

# Panel g draws no HR placebo curve, so that arm has no HR comparison.
max_abs <- function(x) if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else max(abs(x), na.rm = TRUE)
edgar_summary <- cmp_edgar |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arms)) |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    `DBP max abs diff (mmHg)` = max_abs(dbp_diff),
    `DBP median diff (mmHg)` = median(dbp_diff),
    `HR max abs diff (bpm)` = max_abs(hr_diff),
    `HR median diff (bpm)` = median(hr_diff, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(`Dose (mg)` = arm)
knitr::kable(edgar_summary, digits = 2)
```

```{r edgar-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
cmp_edgar |>
  select(arm, time, dbp, dbp_paper, hr, hr_paper) |>
  pivot_longer(c(dbp, dbp_paper, hr, hr_paper)) |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  mutate(
    endpoint = ifelse(grepl("^dbp", name), "Diastolic BP (mmHg)", "Heart rate (beats/min)"),
    source = ifelse(grepl("paper", name), "Fuhr 2022 Figure 4 (digitised)", "nlmixr2lib")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = arm, linetype = source)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = NULL, colour = "Dose (mg)", linetype = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")
```

Replicates Figure 4 panels d and g of Fuhr 2022.

The packaged model reproduces the paper's DBP curves to within about 1 mmHg and
its HR curves to within about 0.7 beats/min. The DBP curves carry a small
systematic offset (the packaged model predicts slightly more decrease) that is
absent from the placebo curve, so it comes from the drug term. The likely cause
is rounding: Table 3 prints EC50 as `0.04` umol/L. Refitting EC50 to the
digitised curves with Emax held at 56.18 gives about 0.044 umol/L, inside the
rounding interval 0.035-0.045. The maintainers did not adjust any value; the
printed parameters are packaged as published. The same refit for HR recovers
`h` = 1.40, EC50 = 0.052 umol/L and Emax = 39.6 beats/min, all consistent with
Table 3. Using `h` = 1.4 for DBP as well would make the DBP curves miss by up
to 4.5 mmHg. That supports reading Table 3 as having no Hill coefficient for
DBP (h = 1).

```{r edgar-gate}
# Deterministic: the only differences are digitisation error and the 2-dp
# rounding of EC50. Measured maxima 1.10 mmHg (DBP) and 0.67 bpm (HR). A
# wrong Hill coefficient (h = 1.4 for DBP) gives 4.5 mmHg, and a
# percent-vs-fraction slip on an amplitude gives tens of mmHg.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(cmp_edgar$dbp_diff)) < 2,
  max(abs(cmp_edgar$dbp_diff[cmp_edgar$arm == "placebo"])) < 0.5,
  sum(!is.na(cmp_edgar$hr_diff)) == 3 * nrow(edgar), # three dosed HR arms
  max(abs(cmp_edgar$hr_diff), na.rm = TRUE) < 1.5
)
```

## Hypertensive patients: Blychert 1990 and Hedner 1986 (panels e, f, h, i)

Panels b and c (the plasma concentrations for these two studies) are raster
images, so the drug curves cannot be driven from a digitised concentration.
Two checks remain:

1. **Placebo curves**, which depend only on the circadian layer and the
   Table S5 parameters (`CEFFECT = 0`).
2. **Cross-endpoint consistency.** The drug-minus-placebo DBP difference of
   panel e (or f) is inverted through the DBP Emax function to the plasma
   concentration it implies. That concentration then drives the HR model, and
   the result is compared with the drug HR curve of panel h (or i). This tests
   whether the DBP and HR curves come from one concentration through the
   Table 3 Emax parameters, and whether hypertensive patients share those
   parameters.

```{r hypertensive}
check_ht <- function(dig, study_mod, study) {
  e_dbp <- pmax(dig$dbp_placebo - dig$dbp_drug, 0)
  conc_implied <- 0.04 * e_dbp / (56.18 - e_dbp) # umol/L, inverse of Eq. S20
  ev <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = dig$time, CEFFECT = 0),
    data.frame(id = 2L, time = dig$time, CEFFECT = conc_implied)
  ) |>
    # DIS_HYPERT stays 0: the study-specific Table S5 means passed to
    # study_model() already are the hypertensive values, and setting it to 1
    # would apply the Table 3 hypertensive ratio on top of them.
    mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, DIS_HYPERT = 0)
  sim <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(study_mod, ev))
  stopifnot(nrow(sim) == 2 * nrow(dig))
  data.frame(
    study = study,
    time = dig$time,
    conc_implied_ngmL = conc_implied * mw,
    dbp_placebo_paper = dig$dbp_placebo,
    dbp_placebo = sim$dbp[sim$id == 1],
    hr_placebo_paper = dig$hr_placebo,
    hr_placebo = sim$hr[sim$id == 1],
    hr_drug_paper = dig$hr_drug,
    hr_drug = sim$hr[sim$id == 2]
  )
}
cmp_ht <- bind_rows(
  check_ht(blychert, mod_blychert, "Blychert 1990"),
  check_ht(hedner, mod_hedner, "Hedner 1986")
)
ht_summary <- cmp_ht |>
  group_by(study) |>
  summarise(
    `Placebo DBP max abs diff (mmHg)` = max(abs(dbp_placebo - dbp_placebo_paper)),
    `Placebo HR max abs diff (bpm)` = max(abs(hr_placebo - hr_placebo_paper)),
    `Drug HR max abs diff (bpm)` = max(abs(hr_drug - hr_drug_paper)),
    `Implied peak conc (ng/mL)` = max(conc_implied_ngmL),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(Study = study)
knitr::kable(ht_summary, digits = 2)

# Deterministic. Measured maxima: placebo DBP 0.26 mmHg, placebo HR 0.01 bpm,
# drug HR 0.26 bpm.
stopifnot(
  all(ht_summary$`Placebo DBP max abs diff (mmHg)` < 0.5),
  all(ht_summary$`Placebo HR max abs diff (bpm)` < 0.5),
  all(ht_summary$`Drug HR max abs diff (bpm)` < 1)
)
```

```{r hypertensive-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
cmp_ht |>
  select(study, time, dbp_placebo, dbp_placebo_paper, hr_placebo, hr_placebo_paper, hr_drug, hr_drug_paper) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(study, time)) |>
  mutate(
    source = ifelse(grepl("paper", name), "Fuhr 2022 Figure 4 (digitised)", "nlmixr2lib"),
    curve = sub("_paper", "", name)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = curve, linetype = source)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~study, scales = "free", ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "mmHg or beats/min", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")
```

Replicates the placebo curves of Figure 4 panels e, f, h and i, and the drug
curves of panels h and i using the concentration implied by panels e and f.
The implied peak concentrations (about 7.8 ng/mL for Blychert 1990 and
6.7 ng/mL for Hedner 1986) agree with the predicted peaks shown in panels b
and c (about 8 and 7 ng/mL). Both checks pass: the circadian layer is
reproduced exactly, and the DBP and HR models are mutually consistent in
hypertensive patients with the shared Table 3 Emax parameters.

# Non-compartmental analysis

Not applicable. The packaged model has no PK layer and no dose records:
felodipine concentration is an input (`CEFFECT`), and the paper reports
no NCA of the PD endpoints. The deterministic checks and the Figure 4
replication above take the place of the PKNCA comparison.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **PD layer only.** The PK-Sim / MoBi whole-body PBPK layer (Table 2) is not
  reproduced, because its organ volumes, blood flows, partition coefficients
  and CYP3A4 expression profile are platform database outputs the paper does
  not print. The felodipine plasma concentration must be supplied as
  `CEFFECT` in umol/L. Divide ng/mL by 384.25 (Table 2 molecular weight), or
  nmol/L by 1000. The DDI scenarios of the paper (Section 3.3) act through
  the PBPK layer. With this model they are reproduced only by supplying the
  DDI-altered plasma concentrations.
* **Hill coefficient for DBP.** Equation 1 / S20 is written with a Hill
  coefficient `h`, but Table 3 and Table S6 list `h` for the HR model only.
  The DBP Emax function is therefore hyperbolic (h = 1). The Figure 4
  replication above supports this reading: h = 1 reproduces panel d to within
  about 1 mmHg, h = 1.4 misses by up to 4.5 mmHg.
* **Amplitudes are fractions.** Table 3 reports the amplitudes in percent
  (2.14 %, 5.93 %, 6.3 %). Equations S17 and S19 multiply the 24 h mean by
  `(1 + circ)`, so they are entered as fractions (0.0214, 0.0593, 0.063). The
  exact match to the placebo curves confirms the scale.
* **Time origin of the phases.** Fuhr 2022 optimised the circadian phases
  against each study's own simulation time (Figure 4 time axes run from the
  first dose, e.g. 336-366 h for day 15). `time` in this model is that
  simulation clock in hours, and the phases are relative to its origin, not to
  midnight. The published phases are not clock times. The Table 3 typical
  phases (5.28 h, 0.16 h and 11.8 h) are means over studies whose dosing
  clock times differed, so they describe a generic study only. To reproduce a
  specific study, override them with its Table S5 values, as done above.
* **Study-specific circadian parameters.** The 24 h means and phases were
  re-optimised for every simulated study (Table S5); Table 3 reports their
  means (SD). The packaged typical values are the Table 3 means. The SDs
  (e.g. 6.76 mmHg for BPmean) describe between-study spread of the optimised
  values, not between-subject variability, and are not encoded as random
  effects. The Table 3 means could not be recomputed exactly from the Table S5
  rows (for example, the healthy-volunteer BPmean rows average 70.9 mmHg
  against the printed 70.4 mmHg), probably because the summary also covers
  simulations not listed in Table S5. The printed Table 3 values are used.
* **Hypertension.** Table 3 gives separate 24 h means for healthy and
  hypertensive individuals (footnote b). These are encoded through the
  `DIS_HYPERT` indicator as log-ratio shifts that reproduce the printed values
  exactly. The paper also reduced CYP3A4 kcat by 32 % on average in
  hypertensive individuals (Results 3.1). That is a PBPK-layer effect and
  reaches this model only through `CEFFECT`.
* **No variability.** No inter-individual variability and no residual-error
  model are reported. Both are zero (`addSd_dbp` and `addSd_hr` fixed at 0),
  so the model gives typical-value predictions of mean DBP and HR.
* **No tolerance.** The paper notes that HR tolerance during multiple dosing
  could not be modelled for lack of data (Discussion). The HR effect is
  therefore the same on every dosing day.
* **Systolic blood pressure** was not modelled by the paper (Discussion).
* **Digitisation.** The Figure 4 curves were extracted from the article's
  vector graphics, with each axis calibrated on its tick marks. Digitisation
  error is a small fraction of 1 mmHg / 1 beat per minute, judged by the
  0.01 bpm agreement on the HR placebo curves.
